To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

concurrent subacute exposure of male rats to low or high dose of arsenic and malation through drinking water and diet, respectively, resulted in differential effects on body weight, liver and liver weight, and activities of hepatic phase I and II enzymes and microsomal or cytosolic proteins.

concurrent subacute exposure of male rats to arsenic and to malathon at groundwater contamination levels and at sublethal concentrations, respectively, resulted in differential effects on body and liver weights and on hepatic drug metabolizing enzymes.

concurrent exposure to arsenic via drinking and malathion in diet in rats produced more adverse effects on body or liver weight, and the biochemical changes were mostly comparable to those caused individually by arsenic or malation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential health risk of concurrent exposure to arsenic in drinking water and malachite via diet.

the effects of concurrent exposure of male rats to subacute arsenic and malation, and the results indicate that the body and liver weights and the drug metabolizing enzymes are differentially affected by concurrent exposure.
the possible toxicological interactions of the co-exposure to arsenic and organophosphates in the context of their environmental occurrence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

concurrent exposure to arsenic (4 ppm or 40  ppm) and malathion (50 ppm or500 ppm) for 28 day in male rats produced a differential effect on the hepatic phase I drug-metabolism and protein content, with the concurrent exposure to the low-dose combination being the most toxic to the liver.

concurrent exposure to arsenic via drinking and malathion in diet is more hazardous to the body and liver weights, while producing biochemical effects that are comparable to the effects caused by the individual agent.
the effects of arsenic and malathan on drug-metabolising enzymes are not additive, but the effect on liver and body weights is additive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arsenic and malation are both capable of causing toxicological effects on hepatic enzymes in rats.
concurrent exposure to low doses of arsenic and malation is more hazardous to body or liver weights, but not to the drug-metabolising enzyme system, than exposure to the individual agents.
the effects of arsenic and malation alone and in combination are not additive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concurrent subacute exposure of arsenic and malanthion is not more hazardous to the hepatic drug metabolizing system in male rats than the single agent.
arsenic and malathon are toxicants and exposure to these agents alone or in combination should be reduced to minimize adverse health effects in humans and other animals.
the combined effects of arsenic and malation on drug-metabolism enzymes in liver of male rats are not additive.
